name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,789

entries.clue: Opponent's for change, not against (10)

indicatorNotes.for change: the letters are offered up to be changed into something else

annotation.surface: Someone describes a rival who has come round to supporting reform.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that an antagonist is exactly the person who is against, so the fodder denies the answer it spells.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name the person on the other side of a fight or argument.

entries.clue: Rude, coarse artist becoming accepted by Society (7)

indicatorNotes.becoming: one part turns into another: the artist becomes the accepted mark

blocks.note: U = upper-class, socially acceptable; put in RA's place

annotation.surface: A vulgar painter somehow wins acceptance among high society.
annotation.walkthrough: 'U' versus 'non-U' was a 1950s label for upper-class and not-upper-class usage; crosswords still use U for acceptable. Swap it for the RA in ABRASIVE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym at the strong end: rude words hurled in anger are abusive ones.

entries.clue: "Excite a little" - that encapsulates it (9)

indicatorNotes.Excite: to excite is to agitate, and agitated letters will not stay in the order given

annotation.surface: A dictionary-style gloss, with a remark that the phrase sums the word up.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: 'excite a little' really does sum up titillate, and the same words stirred round IT build it.
annotation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite mildly, often in a teasing way.

entries.clue: Spears raised regularly during spear song (5)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, lifted means read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so the letters are taken at a steady every-other spacing
indicatorNotes.during: the letters come from inside the phrase that follows

annotation.surface: Warriors lift their spears in time with a battle song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spears' is used twice with different jobs: the first is the definition, a verb; the second is raw letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: a bull's horns pierce the way a spear does.

entries.clue: Note doughnut with new taste, possibly rhubarb (8)

blocks.note: taste is one of the senses

annotation.surface: A baker notes a doughnut with a new flavour, perhaps rhubarb.
annotation.walkthrough: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense, as well as the fruit the surface wants for a doughnut filling.
annotation.definitionFit: Talking rhubarb means talking nonsense.

entries.clue: Copper on radio for so long (3,3)

indicatorNotes.on radio: heard, not seen: the letters are spoken

blocks.note: Cu is copper's chemical symbol, spoken as two letters

annotation.surface: A police officer lingers on the airwaves for ages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' wants to be a policeman on the radio; it is the element Cu, said aloud.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are casual goodbyes.

entries.clue: Clobber game when it retreats (4)

indicatorNotes.when it retreats: an army that retreats goes back the way it came, so the game is read backwards

blocks.note: brag is a card game like poker

annotation.surface: Beat the opposition, then back off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like a verb, to hit; here it is the British noun for clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for clothing or gear, as is garb.

entries.clue: Sailors having a party on top deck (5)

indicatorNotes.on top: in a down clue, the party sits above the sailors

annotation.surface: The crew throw a party up on the top deck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deck' is a verb here, to decorate, not part of a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: Deck in its decorating sense, as in 'deck the halls', is a synonym.

entries.clue: Pirate needing repair to globe (7)

indicatorNotes.needing repair: the letters are broken and must be put back together

annotation.surface: A buccaneer patches up a battered globe, or map of the world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pirate' is an adjective or verb: pirate copies are bootleg copies.
annotation.definitionFit: Pirate and bootleg both describe illegally copied goods.

entries.clue: Dispenser of drams? One article which might replace glasses (8)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for 'one who might replace glasses'

blocks.note: an optic is the upturned-bottle measure behind a bar

annotation.surface: A bar's spirit measure is so handy it might stand in for glasses.
annotation.walkthrough: British pubs pour spirits through an optic, a measure clipped to an upside-down bottle. The surface wants glasses for drinking; the definition means spectacles.
annotation.definitionFit: An optician fits and replaces spectacles.

entries.clue: Remark companion's missed by complete accident (9)

indicatorNotes.missed by: the companion is left out of the word that follows

annotation.surface: Someone notes that a friend's comment went unheard in a total mishap.
annotation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British order; dropping it from CHANCE leaves ANCE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything spoken aloud counts, a remark included.

entries.clue: Still passionate in chamber? (5)

indicatorNotes.in: one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a po is a chamber pot

annotation.surface: Is the ardour still there behind the bedroom door?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' wants to be an adverb; it is a noun, a still photograph. PO is British for a chamber pot.
annotation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, often from a film.

entries.clue: Ticks over icons on mobile? (5)

indicatorNotes.on mobile?: heard down a phone line, so spoken rather than written

blocks.note: icons = idols, said the same way

annotation.surface: A phone user taps checkmarks over the app icons on the screen.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'icons on mobile' about app symbols; the mobile is a phone you speak into, and the icons are idols.
annotation.definitionFit: Motoring idiom: an engine running slowly in neutral both ticks over and idles.

entries.clue: Sensitive English poet originally appointed Laureate (9)

indicatorNotes.originally: take the first letter of each word that follows

annotation.surface: A thin-skinned English poet was first appointed Poet Laureate.
annotation.walkthrough: Andrew Motion was Britain's Poet Laureate, which the surface nods to.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone quickly moved by feelings.

entries.clue: See about crossing Alps getting fresh passes (7)

indicatorNotes.about: as in 'about turn', the word faces the other way
indicatorNotes.crossing: goes across the other word, holding it
indicatorNotes.getting fresh: something freshened is made anew, so the letters come out in a new order

annotation.surface: A traveller crossing the Alps finds fresh mountain passes to see.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passes' is a verb, as time passes, not mountain passes.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym used of time: the weeks slip by, or go past.

entries.clue: Clean egg is in return packaging (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the words go inside the packaging

blocks.note: a nit is a louse's egg

annotation.surface: Wash an egg before it goes into the packaging for return.
annotation.walkthrough: A British SAE is an envelope you send already stamped and addressed so the reply comes back to you, hence return packaging.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym, with the extra sense of killing germs.

entries.clue: Merciless leader restricts team socialising (6)

indicatorNotes.restricts: to restrict is to confine, so the leader's name closes round the team

blocks.note: Ming the Merciless, villain of Flash Gordon
eleven players, as in a cricket or football XI

annotation.surface: A harsh manager stops the players going out together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Merciless leader' looks like it wants M, the first letter; it is a whole character, Ming the Merciless.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a party host hopes guests will mingle and chat.

entries.clue: Halal shin's prepared as God would have it (9)

indicatorNotes.prepared: the letters are made up into something new

annotation.surface: A cut of halal meat is butchered as religious law requires.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface stays in Muslim practice, which is where the answer, Arabic for 'if God wills', comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: Inshallah means 'if God wills it'.

entries.clue: Coinage of novel phrase about Northern Line (8)

indicatorNotes.novel: novel means new, and a new version of the phrase has its letters reordered
indicatorNotes.about: going round, so the new letters surround N

annotation.surface: A new expression coined about London's Northern Line Tube.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coinage' wants a new word, which the surface supports; here it is loose coins, which the British call shrapnel.
annotation.definitionFit: Shrapnel is British slang for small change.

entries.clue: They might be Rick's family mugs (6)

blocks.note: Rick Stein is a British TV chef; think of his surname in the plural

annotation.surface: A chef's relatives are gullible fools.
annotation.walkthrough: Rick Stein is a well-known British TV chef. 'Mugs' reads as fools after 'family', but means beer tankards.
annotation.definitionFit: A stein is a large beer mug, and the Steins would be Rick Stein's family.

entries.clue: Salmon, company reared on island in case of shortage (7)

indicatorNotes.reared: in a down clue, lifted means read upwards
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, sits above
indicatorNotes.in case of: held by the outer letters, the case, of the word

blocks.note: a key or cay is a low island

annotation.surface: A salmon-canning company sets up on an island to guard against shortages.
annotation.walkthrough: Key is the Florida Keys word for a small island. 'In case of shortage' reads as 'in the event of'; here the case is S...E.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the red-fleshed Pacific species is one kind of salmon.

entries.clue: Cutter, when returned, secured by husband and wife (7)

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned is sent back, so the word reads backwards
indicatorNotes.secured by: the couple hold the word fast between them, like a lock

annotation.surface: A married couple lock up a tool once it's been given back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Husband and wife' reads as a couple, but gives H AND W with SA slipped between.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a saw worked by one hand is one kind of cutter.

entries.clue: Eavesdrop on women fronting independent pop-up! (7)

indicatorNotes.fronting: the women and independent go first
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, read upwards

annotation.surface: Snoop on women running an independent pop-up shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pop-up' is split: pop is father, PATER, and up turns it round. Pater is an old British public-school word for father.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: tapping a phone line is electronic listening-in.

entries.clue: One making predictions tipped paddleboat? (6)

indicatorNotes.tipped: loses its tip, the first letter

blocks.note: a small round boat paddled by one person; C removed

annotation.surface: A fortune-teller forecasts that a paddleboat will capsize.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tipped' suggests capsized, which fits a boat; it means the top letter is lopped off.
annotation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a prophet such as the one at Delphi foretold events, hence any predictor.

entries.clue: It's relaxed, with 'ace' fare? (9)

indicatorNotes.relaxed: the letters are loosened and rearranged

annotation.surface: A laid-back eatery with excellent food.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a casual place serving good food.
annotation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is an informal self-service eating place.

entries.clue: Carry on investing roubles in flutter (5)

indicatorNotes.investing: to invest money is to put it into something, so the R goes inside
indicatorNotes.in: the R sits inside the flutter

blocks.note: R, the first letter of roubles, as on price tags

annotation.surface: Keep gambling roubles on a flutter, a small bet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is finance: investing roubles, a flutter as a bet. 'Carry on' means to flirt, as in carrying on with someone.
annotation.definitionFit: British idiom: carrying on means dallying romantically with someone.

entries.clue: Ex-PM in retreat following book (5)

indicatorNotes.following: the retreat comes after the book

annotation.surface: A former prime minister goes into retirement after a memoir.
annotation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was UK Prime Minister 1997-2007. 'In retreat' reads as withdrawing, but 'in' only links.
annotation.definitionFit: Tony Blair is a former British Prime Minister.

entries.clue: Shout half-heartedly downstairs (5)

indicatorNotes.half-heartedly: half of the heart, the middle LL, goes

blocks.note: one of the two middle Ls removed

annotation.surface: Someone calls down the stairs without much enthusiasm.
annotation.walkthrough: BELLOW's heart is LL; losing half of it leaves BELOW.
annotation.definitionFit: An adverb synonym: going downstairs takes you to the floor beneath.

entries.clue: Multiple terms of reference rule out issues (5)

indicatorNotes.out: something ruled out is excluded, so the R leaves the word

blocks.note: a remit is a body's terms of reference; plural
R, the abbreviation for rule, taken out

annotation.surface: Committees with several briefs dismiss certain topics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rule out' looks like a phrase meaning exclude; it splits into R and 'out'. 'Issues' is a verb, not topics.
annotation.definitionFit: To emit is to issue or send out.

entries.clue: Walls of chapel best trimmed with romantic illumination (9)

indicatorNotes.Walls of: a building's walls are its outside, so take the chapel's outer letters
indicatorNotes.trimmed: the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: the walls are C and L, read literally as C AND L
the elite are the best; E trimmed

annotation.surface: A chapel's walls are decorated with soft, romantic lighting.
annotation.walkthrough: The outer letters are C and L, and the 'and' is kept in the answer: C AND L.
annotation.definitionFit: A candlelit room has soft, romantic light.

entries.clue: Swallows perhaps settle nose to tail (4)

indicatorNotes.nose to tail: the front letter moves to the back

blocks.note: a settle is a high-backed wooden bench

annotation.surface: Swallows, the birds, settle in a line one behind the other.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swallows' wants to be birds; it is a verb. A settle is an old wooden seat, so SEAT has its S moved to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: To swallow food is to eat it.

entries.clue: Moor vessel, checking bows essentially in order (10)

indicatorNotes.checking: the OW sits in front of the vessel, holding it back

blocks.note: a fell is a hill or moor in northern England

annotation.surface: A ship is moored with her bows checked and everything shipshape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moor' wants to be the verb, to tie up a vessel; it is a noun, open upland. 'Order' means a society, not tidiness.
annotation.definitionFit: Both name a brotherhood of members bound by shared rules, as in a religious or chivalric order.
